Independent triangle symmetry check: affine-normalize T to a centered equilateral triangle. An affine symmetry of M_q fixes the centroid and preserves its nonzero scalar covariance (scalar by 120-degree invariance), so is orthogonal. Within each of the six open projection-order chambers, write the three vertex projections as 0,p,1 after smooth affine normalization. The support value is 1−(2/3)√[q(1−p)] for p≤1−q, and ((p+1)−2(1−q)√[(1−q)p])/(3q) otherwise, by upper or complementary lower single-vertex caps. The normalized values match through second derivative but the third derivatives at p=1−q are 1/(4q²) and −1/[4q(1−q)]. The ratio p increases or decreases strictly across a chamber (a nonconstant ratio of two linear forms there), so there is exactly one third-derivative transition per chamber. At projection ties the single-vertex expression is symmetric in the two tying projections and smooth. Thus a rotation subgroup acts freely on exactly six marked directions, contains the three vertex rotations, and has order 3 or 6; the latter is possible exactly at half by central symmetry. Reflections already supplied by the vertex permutations then give the full symmetry group: vertex permutations alone off half, and those together with inversion at half. Affine equivariance now gives exactly the asserted triangle fibers.
correctness.rationale: Uniform simplex sections give P(λᵢ≥t)=(1−t)ᵈ. The upper q-tail mean is 1−dq^(1/d)/(d+1); subtracting the complementary upper-tail first moment from 1/(d+1) gives the lower mean. The two prescribed facet systems respectively bound λᵢ from below and above, so substituting these extrema gives precisely the claimed positive least factors. Each maximizing cap is unique up to a null level set, giving exposed contacts. The scaled gap qD_d/d is H(q)=2q−1−q^(1+1/d)+(1−q)^(1+1/d); strict concavity on (0,1/2) between its two zeros and antisymmetry give the signs. Any center must be the unique vertex-permutation fixed point G. The two extrema would then sum to 2/(d+1), impossible except at half, where complementary caps give symmetry. For the limit, use d(1−x^(1/d))→−log x. Strictness in the limit does not follow from the strict signs alone: qD_∞=(1−q)log(1−q)−q log q has second derivative 1/(1−q)−1/q<0 before half and is antisymmetric, which fills the brief limit argument. The triangle proof is valid given the quoted normalized difference-body premise: three unoriented edge vectors reconstruct the triangle up to translation/reflection, area normalization fixes the scale, and the common body centroid fixes the translation. The corollary can also be checked without assuming the inaccessible premise, by the affine symmetry calculation below. Independent quadrature corroborates the cap formula, not the analytic theorem.
